items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: Oh, Pop Celestan played up there.

ctx.x: And did they have other bands at the Pelicans or the other nuns?
Oh yeah, yeah, sure. Who would they be selling? Oh, Pop Celestan played up there. Mm-hmm. Rene played there. Mm-hmm. And, uh, Sidney Dezby played there. Oh, they had bands up there. Mm-hmm.
I'm trying to think of that trumpet player who was a class, right? It couldn't have been somebody like Shelley LaMelle or...

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: Oh, well, Solistan made up his own band.

ctx.x: I was playing clarinet. I was doing clarinet. And what about the name of Earl? His name was Earl Trusclair. He's the first man that ever showed me any finger on a saxophone. We alternated. He showed me my finger on the saxophone and I showed him his finger on the clarinet. And that's the only thing anybody ever showed me about a saxophone. Oh, no. Nobody never showed me nothing about a clarinet, but on the saxophone, that's the only fella ever showed me anything. He showed me how to finger it. And other than…

broke up? Oh, well, Solistan made up his own band. I mean, on the trumpet, when Ridgely. Shatz. Shatz. And was he playing with you at the Pete Hermans? Who, Shatz? Yeah, I forget who you said was there. Yeah, Shatz was on trumpet at Pete Hermans. Uh-huh. Mm-hmm. Okay, he was playing trumpet. What else? I was wondering about, uh, did you ever meet Charlie Parker around Kansas City or St. Louis or any of those places?

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-15
items.q: I believe that was the first time a lot of those guys heard me play clarinet was in Celestan's band at that time.

ctx.x: Did you say P-Ron would play for a special class of people though, huh?

Yeah, he played for the better class of people, see. He played for the doctors and the lawyers and people up here on St. Charles Street, people back in the place and all that kind of people, the higher class of people, see. And they liked that sweet music and slow and waltzes a lot of things, you know, something like that. Well, the average band around here didn't play that, see. Like John Robeshoe and P-Ron. And they had another fellow here called Peter Bocard and his bunch. Now they played all that kind of…
He had a good band. I had a good band.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: We had this contest with Celestan on Sunday night at the Roosevelt.

ctx.x: Oh, we was coming from Bugaloosa. And we played a dance up there that Saturday night. We had this contest with Celestan on Sunday night at the Roosevelt. And we put the music on the running boat or somewhere. The piano player was in charge of it. And he forgot to tie it or something like that. We got into the slide there. I missed the music. And they asked him, I put it on the hood. On the hood. No music. Eleven of us. I let them out at the white kitchen and I went back. All the way back to Bugaloosa looking for…
Who had the arrangement? Was it stock?
